nodes.name: 3D hierarchical dendritic nanoforest-like Ni3Se2 on Ni foam (NF-Ni3Se2/Ni)
Ni foam treatment
nodes.procedure: A piece of Ni foam (30 mm × 10 mm × 0.5 mm) is ultrasonicated with acetone, water, 3.0 M HCl aqueous solution for 5 min, respectively. Then, the Ni foam is rinsed with water and anhydrous alcohol. Lastly, the Ni foam is quickly dried under ambient conditions.

nodes.name: Ni3Se2 nanoforest on Ni foam hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis procedure, a piece of fresh-treated Ni foam (0.0900 g), selenium powder (0.0500 g), H2O (3.0 mL) and ethylenediamine (EDA, 2.0 mL) are added to a Teflon-lined autoclave with a capacity of 20 mL. The mixture is ultrasonicated for 10 min to form a homogeneous suspension around Ni foam. The autoclave is then sealed and heated at 180°C for 5 h. After reaction, the autoclave is cooled down to room temperature naturally. Then, the Ni foam with black precipitates on the surface is taken out of the Teflon-lined autoclave and washed with water and ethanol for six times to remove adsorbed EDA. The final product is dried in a vacuum oven at room temperature for 6 h.

nodes.name: Ni3Se2 microspheres hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiSO4·7H2O (0.0789 g), H2O (3 mL), ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (0.1000 g), NaOH (0.1000 g), Na2SeO3 [0.1 mL, 1 mol/L] and hydrazine hydrate (1.0 mL) are added in sequence to form a transparent solution under vigorous stirring in a 20 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave. The autoclave is then heated at 180°C for 5 h and cooled down to room temperature naturally. The product is washed with water and ethanol for six times, and then dried in a vacuum oven at room temperature for 6 h.

nodes.source_text: Fig. 3a shows the I-R corrected polarization curves... The as-synthesized NF-Ni3Se2/Ni displays an excellent activity with an onset overpotential of 97 mV and a required overpotential of 203 mV for 10 mA cm-2 and 279 mV for 100 mA cm-2. The Tafel slope of NF-Ni3Se2/Ni was 79 mV dec-1. The exchange current density of NF-Ni3Se2/Ni is calculated to be 0.059 mA cm-2... The values of double layer capacitance (Cdl) were measured to be 1.47 mF cm-2 for NF-Ni3Se2/Ni... The polarization curves exhibit ignorable difference before and after 2000 cyclic voltammetric (CV) scans. Additionally, NF-Ni3Se2/Ni owns a nearly unchanged current density over 200 h.

The I-R corrected polarization curves of NF-Ni3Se2/Ni... The overpotential at 20 mA cm-2 is only 242 mV... the overpotential is only 239 mV to reach 10 mA cm-2 at the scan rate of 2 mV/s... The current density of 100 mA cm-2 of NF-Ni3Se2/Ni only requires an overpotential of 353 mV. The Tafel slopes of NF-Ni3Se2/Ni for OER is 144 mV dec-1. The long-term stability measurements of NF-Ni3Se2/Ni reveal that the OER performance remains almost unchanged... for over 17 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show 3D porous structure retained from Ni foam, covered with nanoforest composed of nanotrees (main trunk 2-5 μm, primary branch 500-1000 nm, secondary leaf-like nanostructures 100-300 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1b–d displays the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of the products. As displayed in Fig. 1b, the 3D porous structure has been remained with the surface differing from that of bare Ni foam ... High magnification SEM images (Fig. 1c and d) show the Ni foam is covered with nanoforest composed of nanotrees with main trunk length of 2-5 μm, primary branch length of 500–1000 nm and secondary leaf-like nanostructures with the lateral size of 100–300 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern confirms rhombohedral Ni3Se2 (JCPDS 85-0754) and Ni (JCPDS 04-0850) phases with no impurity peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All the diffraction peaks can be attributed to the rhombohedral Ni3Se2 (JCPDS 85-0754) and Ni (JCPDS 04-0850) with no other impurity phases, indicating the as-obtained products are pure Ni3Se2 on Ni foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF image and STEM-EDS elemental mapping reveal nanotree-like morphology and uniform distribution of Se and Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark field (HAADF) image and the associated scanning transmission electron microscope EDS (STEM-EDS) element mapping images (Fig. 1f) further reveal the nanotree-like morphology and the uniform distribution of Se and Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS measurement (Fig. S4) confirms successful preparation of pure Ni3Se2 on Ni foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energydispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis (Fig. S3) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurement (Fig. S4) confirm the successful preparation of pure Ni3Se2 on Ni foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni3Se2 nanoforest on Ni foil shows complete water spreading in 0.05 s (hydrophilic); Ni3Se2 microspheres on Ni foil shows contact angle of 141.0±3.0° (hydrophobic).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contact angle between water and Ni3Se2 microspheres on Ni foil is measured to be 141.0±3.0° (Fig. 2c and Video S1). In contrast, water can spread out completely in 0.05 s when dropped onto the surface of Ni3Se2 nanoforest on Ni foil (Fig. 2d and Video S2), demonstrating the hydrophility of Ni3Se2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance values measured: 1.47 mF cm^-2 for NF-Ni3Se2/Ni, 1.19 mF cm^-2 for MS-Ni3Se2/Ni, 1.04 mF cm^-2 for Ni foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The values were measured to be 1.47 mF cm^-2, 1.19 mF cm^-2 and 1.04 mF cm^-2 for NF-Ni3Se2/Ni, MS-Ni3Se2/Ni and Ni foam, respectively (Fig. S16 and S17), revealing the higher active surface area of NF-Ni3Se2/Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS analysis (Fig. S3) confirms successful preparation of pure Ni3Se2 on Ni foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energydispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis (Fig. S3) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurement (Fig. S4) confirm the successful preparation of pure Ni3Se2 on Ni foam.
